author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Remove the global PHPStan type aliases.

The `typeAliases` defined in `tests/phpstan/base.neon` only exist for core's own analysis, but the docblocks in `src/` that use them are read elsewhere too. A WordPress release package and the `WordPress/WordPress` repository only include `src/`, and the stubs generated from core (as used by `szepeviktor/phpstan-wordpress`) keep each reference to an alias while losing its definition. Anyone analyzing a plugin or theme against core then gets an unknown type at every use of an alias, unless they define each one themselves.

The `Maybe_Callable` union is now written out at each of its uses, which are mostly functions, where an alias declared on a class cannot be imported. The `Block_Style_Properties` shape is declared with `@phpstan-type` on `WP_Block_Styles_Registry`, which the generated stubs keep, and imported into `WP_REST_Block_Types_Controller`. A note in `base.neon` explains why new aliases should be declared on a class as well, at least until PHPStan supports declaring one outside a class.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14900.
Follow-up to r63451, r63524.

Props westonruter, marian1.
See #65817.

author: adamsilverstein
message:
REST API: only include revisioned meta in revision responses.

Fix an issue where restoring a revision in the editor overwrote meta values that weren't associated with the revision.

Visual Revisions in the block editor, introduced in 7.0, restores a revision by saving the `meta` returned from the revisions endpoint onto the post. That endpoint returned every `show_in_rest` meta key for the parent post type, but only revisioned keys are stored on a revision, so the rest came back as their default (or `null`) and the restore overwrote the post's real values. Unsynced patterns silently became synced, synced patterns failed to restore with a `rest_invalid_stored_value` error, and any other non-revisioned `show_in_rest` key was reset.

Introduce `WP_REST_Revision_Meta_Fields`, used by `WP_REST_Revisions_Controller`, which limits a revision's `meta` and its schema to the keys from `wp_post_revision_meta_keys()`. This matches what `wp_restore_post_revision()` restores from the classic revisions screen, and requires no editor change. Autosave responses follow the same rules, since they are prepared by the revisions controller; autosave requests still accept all of the parent post type's meta. Plugins that write meta onto revisions directly should add those keys with the `wp_post_revision_meta_keys` filter to keep them in responses.

Also fixes https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/84809.

Props dlocc, davidsword, talldanwp, rachelbaker, prasadkarmalkar, umeshnevase.
Fixes #66329.

author: adamsilverstein
message:
REST API: Introduce the `rest_allowed_cors_methods` filter.

Add a filter to `rest_send_cors_headers()` so the `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` header sent with CORS responses can be adjusted. The list of methods is a fixed default and is not derived from the registered routes, so a site serving routes that accept other methods can now advertise them. The filter receives the method list as an array and the request in context, matching the shape of the sibling `rest_exposed_cors_headers` and `rest_allowed_cors_headers` filters, so a plugin can append to or narrow the list rather than restate it. An empty list omits the header. The default output is unchanged.

The filter is seeded from an `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` header already set on the response, limited to the methods in the default list, falling back to the default list itself. A value set through `rest_post_dispatch` was previously discarded: `rest_send_cors_headers()` runs on `rest_pre_serve_request`, after the response's own headers have been emitted, and `header()` replaces by default.

Follow-up to [56096].

Props moonmeister, sudar, TimothyBlynJacobs, aaemnnosttv, westonruter.
Fixes #46992.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Sync PHPStan fixes from Gutenberg.

These fixes were made in Gutenberg while resolving the PHPStan errors in the plugin, ahead of adding PHPStan to its CI, and are brought to core to keep the two codebases in sync. They were developed in:

* https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/68398
* https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/68404
* https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/68405
* https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/68407

The first one fixes a bug in core. Since r56046 the `array_key_exists()` checks in `wp_register_shadow_support()` have lacked their negation, so a block type with shadow support but no `style` or `shadow` attribute never had them registered, while one that already defined them had its definitions replaced, dropping any `default`. Gutenberg already had the negation. Tests are added for the attribute registration.

The others make implicit type conversions explicit in the layout and duotone code, and narrow the types used by `WP_Theme_JSON::get_feature_declarations_for_node()` so that it reports no errors even at PHPStan rule level 10. Since the node comes from `theme.json` data, that method now also checks that a feature is an array before reading its subfeatures. This fixes a fatal error ("Cannot unset string offsets") when a feature's value is a string, such as a `shadow`, and the block's selectors for that feature are a list rather than keyed by subfeature name, since each numeric key then reads a character of the string instead of a subfeature. The baseline entries for the resolved errors are removed.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14862.
Follow-up to r56046, r56058, r56101, r62478, r63426.

Props justlevine, westonruter, poena, ramonopoly.
See #65817.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Code Quality: Correct `argument.unresolvableType` PHPStan errors in `cron.php`.

In `wp_schedule_single_event()` and `wp_schedule_event()`, `$crons` keys are positive integer Unix timestamps. Using `uksort( $crons, 'strnatcasecmp' )` caused PHPStan level 2+ to report unresolvable callback argument types when passing integer keys to a string comparison function.

Replacing `uksort()` with `ksort( $crons )` maintains natural numerical ordering by timestamp without type mismatches or unnecessary docblock type overrides.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14030.

Follow-up to r4289.

Props huzaifaalmesbah.
See #65817.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Code Quality: Remove a redundant `is_wp_error()` check after uploading a plugin or theme.

After a plugin or theme is installed from an uploaded ZIP file in `wp-admin/update.php`, the upload is cleaned up when `$result || is_wp_error( $result )`. A `WP_Error` is an object and therefore always truthy, so the first operand already covers it and the `is_wp_error()` call can never return `true`. PHPStan reports this as `function.impossibleType`.

The condition is reduced to `if ( $result )`, which behaves identically: a failed installation still cleans up the upload, and only `false`, which `WP_Upgrader::run()` returns when filesystem credentials are requested, keeps the upload so it is still there once the credentials are entered.

This empties the `function.impossibleType` baseline, so the file and its entry in `phpstan.neon.dist` are removed.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14778.

Props Soean.
See #65817.

author: peterwilsoncc
message:
Themes: Clarify 'editor-style' vs 'editor-styles' documentation.

WordPress themes can support both `editor-styles` (plural) for the block editor and `editor-style` (singular) for the TinyMCE/classic editors.

This improves the documentation of the `add_editor_style()` and `remove_editor_styles()` functions to use `add_theme_support( 'editor-styles' )` and `remove_theme_support( 'editor-styles' )` to add stylesheets to the block editor.

The tests for theme support are expanded to ensure that the subtle distinction is retained.

Props azaozz, chaion07, desrosj, hellofromtonya, khoipro, oglekler, sabernhardt, sergeybiryukov, soean, sukhendu2002.
Fixes #60826.

author: westonruter
message:
Administration: Refine the admin menu view transitions.

The admin menu's accordion animation sometimes degraded to a plain cross-fade, because a cross-document view transition snapshots the incoming page at its first render, which can happen before the admin menu has finished parsing. A render-blocking `expect` link now holds the first render until `#wpcontent`, the element right after the admin menu, is parsed, so the snapshot always has the complete menu without waiting for the rest of the page. The link is only printed once the View Transitions style has been printed, since an `expect` target that never appears blocks rendering until the whole document is parsed.

The animation itself is also refined. Each menu item's snapshot is clipped to its animating box, so a submenu wipes open or closed in step with the items around it instead of overlapping them. The Collapse Menu button moves with the menu instead of cross-fading. An open flyout fades out while moving with its menu item, instead of being cut off by that clip.

The style is now enqueued from `wp-admin/admin-header.php` instead of on the `admin_enqueue_scripts` action, which `iframe_header()` also fires, so screens without the admin menu no longer load it. As a result, unhooking `wp_enqueue_view_transitions_admin_css()` no longer turns off admin View Transitions. Dequeuing the `wp-view-transitions-admin` style does, and it works in 7.0 as well.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/11912.
Follow-up to r61491.

Props westonruter, b1ink0, zieladam, mukesh27, dhrupo, audrasjb, joedolson, huzaifaalmesbah, jasonsa19, ozgursar, nikunj8866, darshitrajyaguru97.
See #64470.
Fixes #65032.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Modernization: Use `array_any()` and `array_all()` more widely.

This replaces `foreach` loops that return early on the first matching or failing element with `array_any()` and `array_all()`, with no change in behavior. These loops were all added in later features, so they were missed by the conversions in r62550 and r62553.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14618.

author: jorgefilipecosta
message:
REST API: Let routes turn off `_fields`, `_embed` and response links.

Add a `data_processing` option to REST routes and route handlers, so a route can serve its response data as returned. The option is `false` to turn off every feature, or an array with any of the `fields`, `embed` and `links` keys. Every feature is on by default, the handler setting applies over the route setting feature by feature, and turning off `links` also turns off `embed`.
The settings are resolved once, when the request is matched, and stored on the request attributes, the matched handler and the response, where `rest_filter_response_fields()`, `WP_REST_Controller::get_fields_for_response()` and `WP_REST_Server::response_to_data()` read them. They apply to served, enveloped, batched and preloaded requests, and to responses returned by the `rest_pre_dispatch` filter. The index lists the settings of endpoints that turn a feature off.
Response data that is not an array is now served as returned even without the option: `_fields` leaves scalars and objects alone and keeps list items that are not arrays, links are not added to them unless the object implements `ArrayAccess`, and `rest_preload_api_request()` no longer casts preloaded data to an array.
This lets endpoints that own their output schema, such as the abilities run endpoint, return objects, lists and scalar values unchanged.

Props jorgefilipecosta, gziolo.
See #66267.
Fixes #66372.

author: jorgefilipecosta
message:
Abilities API: Name the author of a `core/content-query` post only to users who may see them.

The `core/content-query` ability returned the author's display name and slug for every post the current user can read, and its `author` slug filter named any user of the site.
Return them only to users who may see the author: the author themselves, users who can edit them or list users, and otherwise users who can read a published post of theirs in a post type exposed to abilities, where the ability already returns the author.

Follow-up to [64388], [64680].

See #66268.

author: oandregal
message:
Editor: Fix edge cases in the entity actions and fields APIs.

`_wp_preload_entity_actions()` and `_wp_preload_entity_fields()` assumed
`$paths` was an array, so the editor crashed when an earlier
`block_editor_rest_api_preload_paths` callback returned `null`, `false`,
a string or an object. Empty values are now turned into an array so the
entity paths are still added. Other non-array values, and contexts that
are not a `WP_Block_Editor_Context`, are returned unchanged. `$context`
now defaults to `null`, so calling either function with one argument no
longer throws an `ArgumentCountError`.

Numeric script module ids are now handled as strings. PHP turned them into
integer array keys, so `wp_get_registered_entity_field_modules()` and
`wp_get_registered_entity_action_modules()` could miss them in a strict
comparison and `array_merge()` could renumber them. Both functions now
return a list of entries holding the module id and the ids of the fields
or actions it applies to. This is the shape the REST controllers already
returned, and they now use these results directly. The entity fields
endpoint now returns module ids as strings, matching its schema.

A field registered with the id `'0'` is no longer rejected as empty.

The code duplicated between the two APIs now lives in a new
`entity-utils.php` file:
- `_wp_add_entity_preload_paths()` builds the preload paths for both
  preload callbacks.
- `_wp_add_entity_modules_to_editor_script()` adds the script modules to
  the editor script for both `admin_footer` callbacks. It takes a callable
  rather than the modules, so the registries are still only read on pages
  that load the editor script.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14716.

Props oandregal, jorgefilipecosta.
See #66229, #66343.

author: peterwilsoncc
message:
Themes: Add `label` support to `theme.json` schema.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/13105.

author: westonruter
message:
Formatting: Document `sanitize_key()` as accepting `mixed`.

Since a non-scalar key was made to yield an empty string in r52292 and non-string scalars were again coerced to a string in r52370, `sanitize_key()` handles values of any type, and its tests cover this. Most of its callers pass raw request data or REST parameters, which are untyped, so documenting `$key` as a `string` caused PHPStan to report an error at nearly every call site.

The `sanitize_key` filter is updated to match, as it receives the original key, and its sanitized key is now typed as a lowercase string so that the result of `apply_filters()` agrees with the function's return type. The cast to `string` before `strtolower()` makes the existing coercion explicit without changing behavior. Tests are added for additional non-string types and for the arguments passed to the filter.

This resolves 50 PHPStan errors at rule level 10.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14759.
Follow-up to r13718, r52292, r52370.

See #54160, #65817.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Widgets: Avoid sidebar name collision in `dynamic_sidebar()`.

This ensures that `dynamic_sidebar()` displays the correct sidebar when it has the same ID as the sanitized name of another sidebar registered earlier.

An exact sidebar ID match is now prioritized over a sanitized name match, which may be less accurate.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/12166.

Follow-up to r5474.

Props sainathpoojary, wildworks, alexvorn2, markoheijnen, dilip2615, mosescursor, im3dabasia1, SergeyBiryukov.
Fixes #22116.

author: jorgefilipecosta
message:
Abilities API: Replace the `author_slug` filter of `core/content-query` with an `author` object.

The `core/content-query` ability filtered posts by author through a `where.author_slug` string, while each post returns its author as an `author` object with `id`, `name`, and `slug`. The REST API posts collection filters by author ID, which the ability did not take.
Replace the filter with a `where.author` object that takes the `id` or the `slug` the `author` field returns, so a result's author can be given back as a filter.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14673.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Tests: Use the null coalescing operators in the test suite.

Replaces `isset()` and `array_key_exists()` ternaries that return the tested value or a fallback of `null` or `''` with the null coalescing operator (`??`), and self-referencing `$x = $x ?? $y` assignments with the null coalescing assignment operator (`??=`).

**Why this is safe**

- `??` and `isset()` test the same condition, so the fallback is used in exactly the same cases.
- `array_key_exists()` and `??` only differ for a key that exists with a `null` value. Every converted `array_key_exists()` site falls back to `null`, so both forms return `null` in that case as well.
- `??=` requires PHP 7.4, which is already the minimum supported version.
- No behavior change; this is test-only code.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14616.

Follow-up to r63609, r63633.

Props Soean, huzaifaalmesbah.
See #65819.

author: whyisjake
message:
Security: Keep the previous secret version when a value is saved unchanged.

Saving a secret's current value again demoted it to the previous slot. Settings forms do this on every submit, so a rotation in progress lost the previous value it depends on.

`WP_Secrets_Libsodium_Provider::set()` now treats an unchanged write as a no-op: nothing is stored and `wp_secret_changed` does not fire. The exception is a write that raises `needs_rotation`, such as `wp_import_option_as_secret()` on an option holding the current value. That write is recorded and keeps the previous version.

`WP_Secrets_Provider::set()` now documents that an unchanged write must not discard the previous version, and `WP_Secrets_Provider_Conformance` tests it, so the rule applies to third-party providers too.

Follow-up to [r64337].

Props ravipatel, ericmann, whyisjake.
Fixes #66353. See #66187.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Remove dead code and document bookmark exceptions.

Several `step_*()` methods in the HTML Processor can throw an `Exception` via `insert_virtual_node()` when bookmarks run out. Documenting this with `@throws` shows PHPStan that the generic `catch` in `step()` is reachable, so its `catch.neverThrown` ignore is removed. The existing `identical.alwaysFalse` ignore now covers that `catch` as well, since PHPStan cannot see `$last_error` being set by a call that throws.

Dead code is also removed from `wp-admin/plugins.php`, along with a redundant check in `WP_REST_Users_Controller::check_reassign()`, whose documented types are corrected.

author: westonruter
message:
Build/Test Tools: Add types for dynamic constants in PHPStan.

PHPStan treated many install-dependent constants as fixed values. Those missing from `dynamicConstantNames` took their placeholder value from the PHPStan bootstrap, and listed ones without a type took the type of their only visible definition. For `WP_DEBUG_LOG` that definition was `false`, so the `is_string()` checks for a log file path in `wp_debug_mode()` and `WP_Debug_Data` were reported as impossible.

Every install-dependent constant now has an explicit type, including those the bootstrap had pinned, such as the content and plugin paths, the cookie names, the memory limits, and the timeouts. Each type is what core expects: the values it defines and documents, and that its reads are designed for. Where real-world configurations are known to define wider values, most often by passing `getenv()` through unconverted, a comment notes them along with how core handles them. Widening the types to cover such values instead would require handling invalid configuration at every read.

The bootstrap definitions remain, since PHPStan does not discover constants that core defines inside a function, but their values no longer affect the analysis. The `preg_replace()` results that define the cookie paths are cast to strings to fit their types, and the PHPUnit bootstrap now defines the memory limits as strings to match theirs.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14034.
Follow-up to r61699, r62965, r63191, r63356.

Props rahultank, westonruter.
See #65817.

author: westonruter
message:
HTML API: Use `@link` instead of `@see` for URL references.

In r64436 the `@see` tags pointing to URLs were converted to `@link` across core, since the WordPress inline documentation standards reserve `@see` for references to functions, methods, classes, and hooks. The HTML API was split out of that change so that it could be reviewed by the component's maintainers, and its references to the HTML Standard and other specifications are now converted as well, in both the classes and their tests. Where both tags appear, `@see` is kept ahead of `@link`, per the standards.

Spec references within prose or a list use the inline `{@link}` form instead, since a tag is only recognized at the start of a line and a block-level tag ends the description. In `WP_HTML_Doctype_Info` this had cut the class description short at its first reference, so that the Code Reference rendered the paragraphs after it as the link's text. Those references are now worked into the prose with descriptive link text.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14370.
Follow-up to r63569, r64436.

message:
Twenty Nineteen: Adjust `sass` usage.

This commit:
- Updates `package-lock.json` after `npm audit fix` and `npm dedupe` (which might be done with other `npm` updates anyway).
- Changes the build to run each command sequentially, so `npm run build` does not need to be used twice to update the RTL stylesheet.
- Introduces `sass:string` to prevent deprecation warnings for `unquote()` global built-in.
- Uses `math.div()` to prevent deprecation warnings for `slash-div` calculations.
- Does **not** replace `@import` (yet).

author: jorgefilipecosta
message:
REST API: Use `wp_prepare_json_value_for_client()` for view configs and entity fields.

Removes the private `_rest_cast_empty_objects_from_schema()` helper, so a single function prepares empty objects according to a schema. The view config and entity fields endpoints now call `wp_prepare_json_value_for_client()`, and `WP_REST_View_Config_Controller::cast_empty_objects()` delegates to it. The private helper was added in this release cycle, so it is removed without deprecation.
`wp_prepare_json_value_for_client()` also recurses into the matching `oneOf`/`anyOf` branch and into `patternProperties`, and keeps `[]` when the schema also allows an array. No view config or entity fields schema allows both an object and an array, so the existing responses are unchanged.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14552.

Follow-up to [64503], [64592].

Props jorgefilipecosta, oandregal.
See #66267.

author: jorgefilipecosta
message:
Editor: Remove the unsupported `single` action context.

Removes `single` from the `context` values the entity actions registry supports, leaving `list`. No screen shows the actions of the `single` context, so an action registered with it showed nowhere. Removing it before 7.2 ships keeps the option to add it later with a defined meaning.
An action registered with `single` is now reported with `_doing_it_wrong()`, like any other unsupported value, and `single` is no longer in the `context` enum of the `/wp/v2/entity-actions` schema.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14545.
Synced from https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/85186.

Follow-up to [64517].

Props jorgefilipecosta, oandregal.
See #66343.

author: aaronrobertshaw
message:
Editor: Scope state rules to the block's own element.

Per-instance state styles never applied to a block whose root selector starts with another block's class. List Item registers `.wp-block-list > li`, so scoping swapped `.wp-block-list` for the instance class and produced `.wp-states-xxxx > li`, which matches nothing because the instance class sits on the `li` itself.

A new `wp_get_state_selector_ancestor()` returns the leading compound and its combinator when that compound names a different block, and `wp_build_state_selector()` gains a `$block_name` parameter so the ancestor is kept and the instance class lands on the block's own compound, giving `.wp-block-list > .wp-states-xxxx`. Selectors for nested elements, such as `.wp-block-button .wp-block-button__link`, keep their existing behavior.

This brings in changes from https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/83986.

Developed in: https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14039

Props ramonopoly, talldanwp.
Fixes #66252.

author: aaronrobertshaw
message:
Editor: Add a background clip block support.

Adds a `background.backgroundClip` block support, so a block can paint its background into the border box, padding box, content box or the text itself. Clipping to the text gives blocks a gradient text fill.

The style engine gains the `backgroundClip` definition and a `VALID_BACKGROUND_CLIP_VALUES` constant, `WP_Theme_JSON` gains the setting and style, and KSES allows `background-clip` and its vendor prefixed companions. A color clipped to the text no longer adds the `has-background` class.

Pseudo states and breakpoints that change the clip, or set a text color over a text gradient, now escape the inherited text clip, in both block instance styles and global styles.

This brings in changes from https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/77141, https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/77142 and https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/85057.

Developed in: https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/13491

Fixes #66094.

author: westonruter
message:
Posts, Post Types: Add `pre_wp_count_attachments` filter.

Introduces the `pre_wp_count_attachments` filter to `wp_count_attachments()`, the counterpart of `pre_wp_count_posts`. Returning a `stdClass` object short-circuits the function, skipping the object cache lookup and both of its queries. Since the `counts` cache group is non-persistent, those queries otherwise run on every request that needs the counts, and on a site with millions of attachments the `GROUP BY post_mime_type` aggregate alone can take several seconds. The filter allows the counts to be served instead from a value pre-computed in the background.

Unlike post statuses, the set of MIME types is not known ahead of time, so only a missing trash count is filled in with zero. The filtered value should therefore contain a count for every MIME type matching `$mime_type`, and only those types. As with `pre_wp_count_posts`, the value is not cached and is passed through the `wp_count_attachments` filter.

The `pre_wp_count_posts` filter introduced in r64245 is brought in line with the new one. A filtered value now short-circuits only when it is a `stdClass` object: any other non-null value was previously cast to an object, turning `false` into a nonsensical result, and filling in missing counts on another class can trigger a dynamic property deprecation. Both filters also clone the returned object, so that a callback which keeps it, such as in a static variable, does not have it modified by core or by later callbacks on the `wp_count_posts` and `wp_count_attachments` filters.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14210.
Follow-up to r64245.

Props jdeep, westonruter, peterwilsoncc.
See #66098.
Fixes #66291.

author: adamsilverstein
message:
Media: Enable client-side uploads in the Media Library and modal.

Enable client-side media processing for Uploads from the Media Library grid, the Add New Media File screen and the media modal in the block editor (in supported browsers).

These screens now use the same pipeline as block editor uploads: the original is uploaded through the REST API, sub-sizes are generated in the browser and sideloaded, then the attachment is finalized. `wp_set_up_cross_origin_isolation()` now also isolates the Media Library grid and the Add New Media File screen using Document Isolation Policy. Uploads huse the client-side processing still use the existing progress, tile and error UI.

When client-side processing is disabled, uploads fall back to the classic flow unchanged. Audio files, uploaders that do not post attachments, and JPEG/PNG files while plupload resizing is enabled also stay on the classic path, and a HEIC the browser cannot decode is handed to the server when its image editor supports HEIC. The Customizer, Site Icon picker and classic editor are not isolated and keep classic uploads.

See https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/82409.

Props adamsilverstein, westonruter, andrewserong, sanayasir, arkaprabhachowdhury, logicrays.
Fixes #65661. See #66220.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Upgrade/Install: Explain when automatic updates cannot run.

When automatic updates can't run, the Plugins, Themes, and Updates screens still say “Automatic update scheduled in 6 hours”. The automatic updater skips the update entirely when the site is under version control or when writing files needs FTP credentials, so that scheduled update never happens.

`wp_get_auto_update_message()` now runs the same two checks as `WP_Automatic_Updater::should_update()`, against the same directory, and says why the update won't run instead. Users who can view Site Health get a link to it, since Site Health already explains both cases. On the Updates screen, the core section drops the schedule and the “kept up to date” line in either case.

The checks walk the filesystem, so the plugins and network themes list tables determine the message once per table instead of once per row.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14506.

author: westonruter
message:
Script Loader: Retire script and style concatenation.

Scripts and styles in the admin and on the login screen are no longer concatenated through `load-scripts.php` and `load-styles.php`. Concatenation paid off when browsers opened few connections per host over HTTP/1.1, but it has long been a source of bugs: dependencies outside the default directories were not honored, `SCRIPT_DEBUG` and the `script_loader_src` and `style_loader_src` filters were ignored, inline styles could be duplicated, and code run by the loaders without WordPress loaded caused fatal errors. It was turned off by default in r64320, once the assets of the next admin screen began to be prefetched in r64120, and this removes what remains.

Every item is now printed as its own tag, and what remains of the concatenation API is deprecated or removed:
* The properties of `WP_Scripts` and `WP_Styles` that held items back for concatenation are deprecated but still declared, so plugins reading or setting them keep working. The `do_item()` methods no longer check `do_concat`.
* The `_print_scripts()`, `_print_styles()`, `script_concat_settings()`, `in_default_dir()` and `WP_Dependencies::get_etag()` functions are deprecated.
* The `print_head_scripts`, `print_footer_scripts`, `print_admin_styles` and `print_late_styles` filters only decided whether held markup was printed, so they are applied with `apply_filters_deprecated()` and their return values are ignored.
* The `CONCATENATE_SCRIPTS` constant is no longer read.
* The `wp_should_concatenate_admin_scripts()` function and its filter, added in r64120 for the transition and never released, are removed.

The loaders now respond with 410 Gone and a one-line plain text explanation, without loading WordPress, so that requests from bots and stale links cost next to nothing. Code written to run inside them without WordPress loaded, such as `wp_theme_has_theme_json()`, now uses the functions it had avoided, and `wp-admin/includes/noop.php` no longer defines its stub functions.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14463.
Follow-up to r10357, r43580, r60719, r62657, r64120, r64320, r64485.

Props westonruter, jonsurrell, peterwilsoncc, azaozz, markhowellsmead, sergiomdgomes, jerclarke, adamsilverstein, sukhendu2002, adnan007, momo360modena, desrosj, welcher.

author: westonruter
message:
Upgrade/Install: Report fatal errors in auto-update emails.

When a plugin auto-update was rolled back because the loopback request found a fatal error, the failure email gave no reason, even though `WP_Automatic_Updater::has_fatal_error()` had already received the error's message, file, and line in the scrape result. These details are now added to the rollback `WP_Error` under a new `plugin_update_fatal_error` code, so the email lists them under the plugin whose update failed. This works regardless of `WP_DEBUG`, and when the loopback request itself fails, its error message is reported instead, so a rollback is no longer left unexplained.

The details are carried on the plugin's update result rather than in a transient, so that they cannot expire during a long update run, go stale when no email is sent, or be attributed to the wrong plugin when several fail in the same run. This also leaves the signature of the protected `has_fatal_error()` method unchanged for subclasses. Only the first line of the error message is included, since the message for an uncaught exception continues with a stack trace whose argument values, such as database credentials, would otherwise leave the server by email.

The parameters of the `send_plugin_theme_email()` and `after_plugin_theme_update()` methods are also typed with the update result types, so that PHPStan can check the new email code, which resolves a baselined error for a possibly undefined `$subject`.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/10445.
Follow-up to r58128, r64435.

author: westonruter
message:
Build/Test Tools: Report PHPStan errors in a pull request comment.

Since PHPStan was integrated into CI, its errors have only been reported as warning annotations, which are easy to miss, even for committers. Some cannot be shown alongside the changes at all: an out-of-date baseline entry is reported without a line number, which is how a stale baseline was committed in r63485 and regenerated afterward in r63486, and an unmatched `ignoreErrors` entry without a path has no file to be attached to.

The annotations are now emitted from PHPStan's JSON report instead of by `cs2pr`, since that report says whether each error can be ignored. Errors that can be ignored remain warnings, while those PHPStan does not allow to be ignored are annotated as errors and fail the check, with instructions for regenerating the baselines when those are the cause.

For pull requests, the results are also uploaded as an artifact, which a new workflow triggered by `workflow_run` turns into a single comment on the pull request, so that it works for pull requests from forks as well. The comment's heading shows whether the check fails, has only warnings, or has nothing left to report. It lists each error with the commit it was first reported for, moves the errors that a commit resolves into a collapsed list naming that commit, and is minimized once all of them are resolved. The history is kept within the comment itself. Since the analysis runs on the pull request merged into its base branch, errors in files that the base branch has changed since are not linked to their lines, and the comment suggests merging the latest base branch instead.

The artifact is treated as untrusted: nothing from the pull request is checked out in the privileged workflow, the results are validated, messages are rendered as code spans so that they cannot mention users or link issues, and results are only accepted for the current head of the pull request.

The PHPStan README now describes these results, and discourages `@phpstan-ignore` comments, which hide an error from every later analysis of that line, in favor of fixing the error or correcting the types PHPStan relies on.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14261.
Follow-up to r61699, r63019.

See #65817.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Narrow types for REST requests and responses.

Adds array shapes and narrowed types to `WP_HTTP_Response`, `WP_REST_Request` and `WP_REST_Response`, and to the parts of `WP_REST_Server` that pass data to them, reusing the route handler and endpoint argument aliases the server already defines. Several existing types were wrong rather than merely loose, and are corrected:

* A request's body is null until one is set.
* A request's JSON params decode to a scalar for a JSON body that is not an object or array.
* A request's headers hold lists of values.
* A file param may describe a failed upload, or a field named with brackets such as `files[]`.

The status code is typed `int<100, 599>`, and `absint()` gains a template conditional return so that an argument already known to be a non-negative integer keeps its narrower type through it. The one call where that type cannot be inferred, in the deprecated numeric branch of `wp_get_recent_posts()`, is added to the PHPStan baseline. The no-cache check for a 4xx response to a method-overridden request now compares the status numerically instead of passing an integer to `str_starts_with()`, which removes another baseline entry, and a test now covers that path.

The narrower types also expose existing bugs that are left for follow-up: a scalar JSON body makes `WP_REST_Request::set_param()` fatal and `WP_REST_Request::sanitize_params()` warn, and uploading to the media endpoint with a `file[]` field makes `WP_REST_Attachments_Controller::create_item()` throw a `TypeError`.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14471.
Follow-up to r34928, r56834, r57126, r62618, r63646, r63756.

Props westonruter, apermo.

author: adamsilverstein
message:
REST API: Send URL sideloads through the shared attachment insert path.

Since [62659], a `POST /wp/v2/media` request with a `url` built its own response in `create_item_from_url()` and returned before `create_item()` did any of its work. Fields the schema accepts (`title`, `caption`, `description`, `alt_text`, `featured_media`, `meta`, terms) were silently dropped. The `rest_pre_insert_attachment`, `rest_insert_attachment` and `wp_after_insert_post` hooks never fired. A request with both an uploaded file and a `url` discarded the file without an error.

This treats a URL as a third source of the file, next to a multipart upload and a raw request body. `create_item_from_url()` becomes `upload_from_url()`, a sibling of `upload_from_file()` and `upload_from_data()`. It downloads the remote file, passes it to `wp_handle_sideload()`, and returns the same data. `insert_attachment()` picks the handler, so every path now shares the same insert, hooks and field handling. A request with both a file and a `url` now returns a 400. An error returned from `rest_pre_insert_attachment` is now respected on every path instead of being used as if it were an attachment.

Follow-up to [62659], [62841].

Props jeremyfelt, andrewserong, khokansardar.
Fixes #65810.

Editor: Remove theme.json preset items of unexpected types to prevent fatals in PHP

It does this by removing theme.json preset items that aren't objects, or whose `slug` isn't a scalar, in `WP_Theme_JSON::sanitize()`.

Previouly, for example, a preset list of strings, such as `"fontFamilies": [ "Inter" ]`, failed with `Cannot access offset of type string on string` when the stylesheet is generated.

author: adamsilverstein
message:
Media: Generate animated image sub-sizes by default.

Add a `wp_generate_animated_image_subsizes` filter (boolean, default true) so the client pipeline can keep or drop the animation in sub-sizes. The client-side consumption ships via the Gutenberg package updates in https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/80385.

Fixes #65656, #28474.

author: adamsilverstein
message:
Media: stop adding crossorigin attributes in the editor.

Fix an issue where editing a post in Chromium 137+ could end in a fatal error and a blank screen when the page loaded any cross-origin resource. `wp_add_crossorigin_attributes()` ran `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor` over the whole document inside an `ob_start()` display handler, where errors cannot be caught. The injected `crossorigin="anonymous"` was not needed in the first place: `Document-Isolation-Policy: isolate-and-credentialless` loads cross-origin scripts, stylesheets, audio and video without credentials instead of blocking them, and forcing a CORS request broke any host that does not send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, such as media offloaded to a CDN.

The header is now sent directly by the new `wp_send_document_isolation_policy_header()`, and the editor page is no longer buffered or rewritten. `wp_start_cross_origin_isolation_output_buffer()` and `wp_add_crossorigin_attributes()` are deprecated; the first only sends the header and the second returns the HTML unchanged. `wp_print_media_templates()` no longer adds the attribute to AUDIO and VIDEO tags. Cross-origin isolation and client-side media processing are unaffected.

Follow-up to [61844], [62048], [62819].

Props b0b3k, khokansardar, arkaprabhachowdhury, westonruter, andrewserong, algorithmsunlocks, sabernhardt, swissspidy, adamsilverstein.
Fixes #65930. See #65673.

author: adamsilverstein
message:
Editor: Add emoji reactions ❤️ 🎉 😄 👀 🚀 

Add a `reaction` comment type so users can react to a note with one of five emoji. Each reaction is stored as its own comment under the note, with `comment_content` holding the emoji's hex key rather than raw emoji bytes, since the comments table isn't guaranteed to be utf8mb4.

Reactions are created and deleted through the `/wp/v2/comments` endpoint using the note permission checks (`edit_post` on the note's post). They are always approved and authored by the current user, limited to one per emoji per user per note, and cannot be edited. Notes gain a read-only `reaction_summary` field, prefetched in at most two queries per page of notes.

Reactions are excluded from the admin comments list, comment counts, `get_lastcommentmodified()`, comment feeds and a note's `children` link, and are trashed and deleted along with their note. Restoring a trashed note does not yet restore its reactions, see https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/84202.

This brings over the PHP changes from https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/76767.

Props adamsilverstein, wildworks, westonruter, noruzzaman, mamaduka, swissspidy, joedolson, joen, jeffpaul, andraganescu, mciampini, fcoveram, scruffian, manzoorwanijk, annezazu, ellatrix, jorbin.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Database: Ignore default integer display widths in `dbDelta()` on MariaDB.

`dbDelta()` compares the column type in a `CREATE TABLE` query with the type `DESCRIBE` reports. MariaDB, and MySQL before 8.0.17, add a default display width to an integer column declared without one, so a column declared as `bigint unsigned` reports `bigint(20) unsigned`, and `dbDelta()` sends the same `ALTER TABLE` on every call. Likewise, `INTEGER` never matches the `int` the server reports.

This commit skips the change when the query has no width and the server reports exactly the default width for that type, and treats `INTEGER` as `int`; any other difference is still compared, and MySQL 8.0.17+ keeps its existing code path, similar to the 6.1 change in #49364.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14353.

Follow-up to r53897, r60789.

Props jmdodd, janjakes, SergeyBiryukov.
Fixes #46145.

author: westonruter
message:
Script Loader: Remove the unused compression test.

The compression test ran on admin screens until it stored its result in the `can_compress_scripts` option, but that result has had no effect since PHP compression was removed from `load-scripts.php` and `load-styles.php` in r43580, and the last code reading it was removed in r64485. The test also failed with a 400 error when `admin_url()` was filtered to add a query string, as translation plugins do, since it appended a second `?` to the AJAX URL. Users without `manage_options` were sent the test on every admin page, since the AJAX handler rejected their requests and the option was never set. Rather than fixing the URL, the test is removed.

The `compression_test()` and `wp_ajax_wp_compression_test()` functions are deprecated as no-ops so that existing callers do not cause fatal errors, and the `wp-compression-test` AJAX action is no longer registered. On single sites, the option is already deleted on a database upgrade since it is in the list of unused options. On multisite it is a network option, so it is no longer primed and is now deleted by `upgrade_network()`, with the database version bumped for that step.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14412.
Follow-up to r10357, r43580, r64485.

Props azaozz, juzar, tofandel, szepeviktor, irozum, oglekler, peterwilsoncc, westonruter.
See #57548, #63017.
Fixes #58302, #65750, #65980.

author: westonruter
message:
Script Loader: Remove obsolete compression constants.

Even so, the `COMPRESS_SCRIPTS`, `COMPRESS_CSS` and `ENFORCE_GZIP` constants were still documented and read, only to set that unused argument on the loader URLs. That code and documentation are removed.

The `$compress_scripts` and `$compress_css` globals are kept for backward compatibility with code that reads them, but they now default to false since nothing is compressed, and a value already set by a plugin is still left alone. The compression test, which still runs in the admin, is to be removed separately.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/8409.

author: jorgefilipecosta
message:
Connectors: Preload the screen's REST API responses.

The Connectors screen requested the site settings, the `OPTIONS` response of the plugins endpoint, and the records of the AI plugin and of each connector's plugin only after its scripts loaded, which delayed its first render.
Adds the private `_wp_connectors_preload_paths()` callback to the `wp_options_connectors_wp_admin_preload_paths` filter, so these responses are embedded in the page. Only successful responses are preloaded, so the screen still requests the records of plugins that aren't installed.
The filter is applied by the page that the Gutenberg build generates, so the preloading takes effect once the pinned Gutenberg version includes https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/77353.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/11790 and https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/77353.

Fixes #65215.

author: jorgefilipecosta
message:
REST API: Correct the `action-unfiltered-html` link's target schema.

The target schema of the `https://api.w.org/action-unfiltered-html` link description object nested `raw` directly under `content`, without the `type` and `properties` keywords. `raw` isn't a JSON Schema keyword, so the schema put no constraint on `content`.
Wraps `raw` in an object schema, like the `content` property of the post schema, and adds a test for it.

Props jorgefilipecosta.

author: westonruter
message:
Docs: Use `@link` instead of `@see` for URL references.

The WordPress inline documentation standards for PHP and JavaScript reserve `@see` for references to functions, methods, classes, and hooks, and use `@link` for URLs. While phpDocumentor and JSDoc both accept a URL in `@see`, core had used both forms for external references such as specifications, Trac tickets, and GitHub pull requests, so the remaining `@see` tags pointing to URLs are converted to `@link` across core, the bundled themes, core scripts, and the unit tests.

On the touched lines, `@see` is kept ahead of `@link` where both appear, per the standards; links to developer.wordpress.org pages for core functions in Twenty Twenty become `@see` references to those functions; and links that no longer resolve are updated. The block files synced from Gutenberg, the bundled pomo library, and other third-party code are left unchanged, and the HTML API is handled separately.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/10804.
Follow-up to r63569.

Props huzaifaalmesbah, westonruter, noruzzaman, shailu25.
See #65860.

author: westonruter
message:
Upgrade/Install: Add PHPStan types to the automatic updater.

The update offers and results handled by `WP_Automatic_Updater` are now typed by update type, with a type alias for each kind of offer and result and a conditional return type for `WP_Automatic_Updater::update()`. A conditional parameter type for the offer would be preferable, but PHPStan only narrows the outermost condition of a nested conditional parameter type and resolves the others to `never`, so the offer is instead narrowed with inline tags in each branch that reads it, alongside comments to replace them once nested conditions are supported.

Typing the results showed that several documented return types never matched the code. The `null|WP_Error` documented for `update()` since r32655 omitted both the `false` returned when an update is declined and the result passed through from the upgrader. Because `Plugin_Upgrader`, `Theme_Upgrader` and `Language_Pack_Upgrader` redeclare `$result` without a default, their `upgrade()` methods and the plugin and theme `install()` methods return `null` when the operation fails before the package is installed, which their documentation has omitted since r30758. The `$update` parameter of `Language_Pack_Upgrader::upgrade()` is also corrected to the update offer object that its callers pass.

Variables that PHPStan reported as possibly undefined are initialized, and a redundant `$is_debug` assignment from r58139 is removed. This resolves 7 baselined errors across the `argument.type`, `return.type` and `variable.undefined` identifiers.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14361.
Follow-up to r11005, r25566, r30758, r32655, r58139, r63019, r63022, r63024.

See #65817.

author: westonruter
message:
Widgets: Use booleans in Categories widget arguments.

The Categories widget passed `show_count` and `hierarchical` to `wp_list_categories()` and `wp_dropdown_categories()` as the numeric strings `'0'` and `'1'`, while both functions document these arguments as `bool|int`. They are now passed as booleans, matching what the Categories block already passes. Core only checks these values for truthiness, so output is unchanged; a callback on the `widget_categories_args` or `widget_categories_dropdown_args` filter that compares them strictly to `'1'` or `'0'` is the only code affected, which is noted in the filters' `@since` tags.

The arguments passed to those filters, along with the widget's display arguments and instance settings, are now documented as hashes so that static analysis can type them. The `count`, `hierarchical` and `dropdown` settings are documented as the `0` or `1` that `update()` stores, while `widget()` keeps reading them loosely for instances saved before WordPress 2.8, which stored booleans. A missing title in the submitted settings no longer triggers an undefined array key warning in `update()`, which can happen when REST API form data omits it.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/8071.
Follow-up to r10809, r41685, r64331.

Props westonruter, marian1.
See #65817, #65860.
Fixes #62762.

author: jorbin
message:
Rewrite Rules: Add support for random content redirects.

Introduce a `random` query var and `/random/` rewrite rules[1], built on the existing rewrite, WP, and query APIs, that redirect to a randomly selected published post. Random requests[2] work for the whole site, taxonomy terms, authors and post type archives, with the base configurable on the Permalinks screen. A new `randomable` post type argument controls which content is eligible, and the selection runs through the main query so it remains filterable and costs a single database query.

The Random Base[3] is translatable and stored in the rewrite rules. This means that rewrite rules are regenerated when translations are updated or the Site Language is changed. Also, if a post or page is published that would result in the same slug as the Random Base, that content gets priority and nothing will be random[4].

This reintroduces the feature committed in r63767 and reverted in r63906.

1) Literally `/random/`, not just rules that are random. Though that could be fun too!
2) Not "random" as in unpredictable, but random as in someone wanted it to be random.
3) It's intentionally "random" but it could also intentionally be "aleatoria" or "karkovice".
4) The other random permalinks will still work, so not nothing. But is anything really random?

Developed in: https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14018

Follow-up to r63767, r63906.

Props jorbin, peterwilsoncc, westonruter, mukesh27, annezazu, mlaetitia, mcsf, johnbillion, TobiasBg, solankisoftware, sajib1223, ellatrix, matt.

author: luisherranz
message:
Interactivity API: Add server-side processing for the `data-wp-html` directive.

Adds server-side processing for the `data-wp-html` directive, whose client implementation was added in Gutenberg, so that trusted HTML produced in PHP is present in the server-rendered page.

The new `wp_interactivity_as_dangerous_html()` function returns a `WP_Interactivity_Dangerous_HTML` token that marks an HTML string as trusted. Only these tokens render. The HTML is neither sanitized nor processed for directives, and it is never included in the data printed for the client, where a token is encoded as `{}`. An unserialized token holds no HTML and does not render.

When the directive cannot render, the element keeps its existing content and a `_doing_it_wrong()` notice is raised. That happens when the value is not a token, when the element cannot hold content, or when the element also uses `data-wp-text` or `data-wp-each` on a `template`.

Also adds `WP_Interactivity_API_Directives_Processor::set_raw_content_between_balanced_tags()`, which replaces the content between balanced tags without escaping it.

Props darerodz.
Fixes #66246.

Editor: Skip auto-attaching media when attachment pages are enabled.

the old attachment page URL then returns a 404.

This adds an `autoAttachMediaEnabled` setting to `get_default_block_editor_settings()`. It is `false` when the `wp_attachment_pages_enabled` option is on, and `true` otherwise. Sites can still change it with the
`block_editor_settings_all` filter.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Correct nullable `WP_Http_Cookie` property types.

A cookie created without a name, value, domain, expiration or host-only flag, or from incomplete data, leaves those properties `null`, and an unparsable expiration date is stored as `false`, but their documented types said otherwise. PHPStan therefore treated `isset()` checks on them as always true, so correcting the types retires the `booleanOr.alwaysFalse` baseline entirely along with several `isset.property` entries.

The corrected types surfaced real errors in callers, which are fixed rather than baselined:
* In `WP_Http::normalize_cookies()`, a `WP_Http_Cookie` value was passed to `WpOrg\Requests\Cookie` as is, which throws an `InvalidArgument` exception for anything but a string, failing the request. A cookie without a value or with a non-scalar value is now skipped, as `WP_Http_Cookie::getHeaderValue()` already does, and other scalar values are cast to strings.
* `wp_remote_retrieve_cookie_value()` now returns an empty string instead of `null` for a cookie without a value.

The handling of empty or missing cookie names is unchanged, as it is being addressed separately in #66305.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14283.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Remove redundant checks in `human_time_diff()`.

Each branch of the `if`/`elseif` chain that chooses the unit of the time difference checked a lower bound that was already guaranteed by the previous branch not matching. These checks are removed, and the last branch becomes an `else`, which makes it explicit that `$since` is always set before it is passed to the `human_time_diff` filter. For the same reason, the `<= 1` clamps in the minute through year branches could never change the value, so they are removed too; only the seconds branch keeps its clamp, since a zero difference is still reported as "1 second". The result of `round()` is now cast to `int`, so that `_n()` receives the type it declares; the clamps had previously hidden this mismatch from PHPStan by making the type `float|int`.

There is no change in behavior. New tests cover each unit threshold, both exactly at the threshold and one second below it, in both directions. This resolves the remaining errors in the `greaterOrEqual.alwaysTrue` PHPStan baseline, which is deleted.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14005.
Follow-up to r24582, r45573.

author: whyisjake
message:
Security: Introduce the Secrets API.

Credentials such as API keys and tokens are usually stored as plaintext options, so anyone with a database dump or backup can read them. The Secrets API gives plugins and core a place to store them encrypted instead, using `wp_set_secret()`, `wp_get_secret()`, `wp_delete_secret()` and related functions. Each secret keeps its previous version, so a credential can be rotated without breaking the code that reads it.

By default, secrets are encrypted with libsodium and stored in the options table. The encryption key never goes in the database: it comes from a `WP_SECRETS_KEY` constant in `wp-config.php`, or is derived from the `LOGGED_IN_KEY` and `LOGGED_IN_SALT` constants when that is not defined.

Hosts can use a different method by adding a `wp-content/secrets.php` drop-in, which loads just before must-use plugins, in the same way `object-cache.php` replaces the object cache. A drop-in can hand all storage to an external secrets manager, or replace only where secrets are stored or only where the encryption key comes from, such as a key management service. If a drop-in is broken, every Secrets API call returns a `WP_Error` rather than falling back to the default method, so a misconfigured host shows up as an error rather than as secrets that appear not to exist. Conformance test suites are included for drop-in authors.

Also adds the `manage_secrets` capability, granted to administrators through `populate_roles_720()` and `upgrade_720()`, the `manage_network_secrets` meta capability for super admins, and Site Health tests for the Secrets API.

This provides the encrypted storage requested in #64789, so the Connectors screen's API keys can move off plaintext options in a follow-up. The admin screen is deferred to 7.3, and the WP-CLI commands stay in the feature plugin.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Mark `current_user_can()` and `chmod()` as "impure".

PHPStan infers `current_user_can()` and `WP_Filesystem_Base::chmod()` as pure, so it remembers what each returned and reuses that value at a later call in the same scope, reporting the second check as always true or always false. Yet a capability check can legitimately answer differently the second time, since it reads the current user and applies the `user_has_cap` filter, so a plugin hooked in between (for example during the `admin-header.php` load in `wp-admin/link-manager.php`) can change the result. Similarly, `chmod()` changes the permissions that a following `is_writable()` reports. The annotation goes on the call that invalidates the remembered value rather than on read-only accessors like `is_writable()`, and on `current_user_can()` itself since annotating `WP_User::has_cap()` cleared nothing. This resolves 13 baselined errors across five identifiers.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/13074.
Follow-up to r63023, r63301, r63357, r64335.

Props tstokes8040.
See #65817.

author: westonruter
message:
Code Quality: Annotate `WP_HTML_Processor::next_token()` as "impure".

PHPStan infers `WP_HTML_Processor::next_token()` as pure, so the result of `is_tag_closer()` before the matching-closer loop in the block bindings processor's `replace_rich_text()` method survives across the loop, even though each `next_token()` call advances the parser to a different token. The `||` in the check after the loop is then reported as always true, the negation within it as always true, and the code that follows as unreachable. Adding `@phpstan-impure`, as was done for `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::next_tag()` in r61934 and for `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::parse_next_tag()` in r63301, resolves all three baselined errors.

This empties the `booleanOr.alwaysTrue` baseline, so the file is removed along with its `includes` entry in `phpstan.neon.dist`.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14037.
Follow-up to r61934, r63023, r63301.

author: westonruter
message:
Site Health: Stop listing obsolete compression constants.

The `COMPRESS_SCRIPTS` and `COMPRESS_CSS` constants are no longer listed under WordPress Constants on the Info tab. Listing them suggested a setting that still mattered. author: westonruter
message:
Script Loader: Disable script/style concatenation by default.

Scripts and styles in the admin and on the login screen are no longer concatenated by default. When the `CONCATENATE_SCRIPTS` constant is not defined, `wp_should_concatenate_admin_scripts()` now returns `false`, so `load-scripts.php` and `load-styles.php` are only used when a site opts in with `define( 'CONCATENATE_SCRIPTS', true )`. This is the next step toward retiring concatenation. It also puts into effect the prefetching of the admin's assets added in r64120, which only applies when concatenation is off. With an empty browser cache, logging in and then opening the Dashboard, the Posts list and the block editor was measured to be faster this way than with concatenation on.

TinyMCE is now always registered as two separate files instead of the prebuilt `wp-tinymce.js` bundle: TinyMCE core and the compat3x plugin. The bundle was registered only when scripts were both concatenated and compressed, and since r43580 and r44651 the `$compress_scripts` global has not compressed anything, so the registration no longer depends on either. The block editor loads TinyMCE on every screen but initializes it only when a Classic block is edited, so it now downloads 369 KB for the two files instead of 671 KB for the bundle, which also holds the theme and all 22 plugins. When TinyMCE is initialized, in the classic editor or for a Classic block, it now requests them itself and takes longer to become ready, a cost deemed acceptable since the role TinyMCE is increasingly diminished. A site can still register the bundle under the `wp-tinymce` handle. The unused second parameter of `wp_register_tinymce_scripts()` is deprecated.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/13090.
Follow-up to r43580, r44114, r44651, r64120.

See #57548, #66053.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Docs: Allow `false` in the documented type of `WP_REST_Posts_Controller::$allow_batch`.

`WP_REST_Posts_Controller::$allow_batch` is documented as `array`, while `WP_REST_Attachments_Controller`, `WP_REST_Font_Faces_Controller` and `WP_REST_Font_Families_Controller` override it with `false` to opt out of batching. PHPStan reports this as a PHPDoc type that is not covariant with the parent.

`false` is a supported value, as documented for the `allow_batch` route option in `WP_REST_Server` (`array{v1?: bool}|false`). `WP_REST_Server::serve_batch_request_v1()` explicitly handles this value, rejecting the request with `rest_batch_not_allowed` when `allow_batch` is not an array. The parent type is therefore widened to `array|false` to match. This is a documentation-only change.

This resolves all three errors in the `property.phpDocType` PHPStan baseline, which is deleted.

author: westonruter
message:
HTML API: Restore spec-mirroring structure in HTML Processor.

Some code in `WP_HTML_Processor` is written to mirror the steps of the HTML specification, so that it can be compared against the living standard as it changes and extended as more of it is supported. Static analysis reports parts of that structure as unreachable or redundant, which is accurate but beside the point. In r64250 two such places were restructured to satisfy PHPStan: the `else` branch for a `FORM` end tag in `step_in_body()`, which corresponds to the specification's "Otherwise" steps, and the `is_tag_closer()` checks for end tags in `step_in_foreign_content()`, which spell out the specification's "An end tag whose tag name is…" conditions. Both are reverted, along with the trailing `bail()` calls those methods need again.

The errors these intentional constructs produce, along with a false positive where PHPStan does not see that `bookmark_token()` sets `$last_error` before throwing, are now ignored in the HTML API section of `phpstan.neon.dist` with an explanation, rather than left in baselines that invite contributors to fix them. The remaining baseline errors for the HTML API are genuine and are fixed:

* The bookmark counter is cast to a string before being passed to `set_bookmark()`.
* The `$node` variable is initialized before a loop that may not iterate.
* The `$is_closing_tag` property is documented as nullable.
* Redundant `isset()` checks on the always-set `WP_HTML_Text_Replacement::$text` property are removed.

This empties the `catch.neverThrown` baseline, which is deleted.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14141.
Follow-up to r58779, r58871, r64250.

Props westonruter, dmsnell.
See #65817.

author: dmsnell
message:
KSES: Only serialize non-empty block JSON attributes.

In r64255 `wp_kses()` completely reserializes every block delimiter, including any JSON attributes. Unfortunately, if a delimiter contained no JSON attributes, but still presented an empty JSON map, these attributes would be re-serialized as an empty list due to the ambiguity of empty PHP arrays. This led to blocks no-longer parsing as blocks.

    wp_kses( '<!-- wp:block {} -->' ) // turns into `<!-- wp:block [] -->`

This patch checks if any attributes exist before serializing them into the block delimiter. There is a pre-existing version of this problem in WordPress for block JSON attributes whose value is an empty map, but r64255 did not change how those are modified through `wp_kses()`.

Developed in: https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14136
Discussed in: https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/66208

author: westonruter
message:
HTML API: Remove unreachable code from HTML Processor.

The `bail()` method in `WP_HTML_Processor` always throws, and it has been documented as returning `never` since r61699. The `return false;` sentinels added after its calls in r59001, the `break` statements following a `goto`, and the trailing `bail()` calls at the end of methods whose every path already returns could therefore never run, and PHPStan reported them as unreachable. They are removed. Where a sentinel guarded against a future code path falling off the end of a method, PHPStan now catches that case instead by reporting a missing return.

In `step_in_foreign_content()`, end tags are now handled in an `else` branch rather than by re-checking `is_tag_closer()`, which was always true at that point. This lets both PHPStan and IDEs see that every path returns, so the trailing `bail()` is no longer needed.

The remaining `break` statements after a `bail()` call in a `switch` are kept. PHPCS cannot tell that `bail()` never returns, so without a `break` it treats the case as falling through and misreports the indentation of the comment above the next case. They remain in the baseline, along with two other unreachable statements which mirror steps of the HTML specification.

The outer loop of the adoption agency algorithm is likewise kept, along with its safety budget, as scaffolding for the parts of the algorithm which are not yet supported. Since r64237 PHPStan has reported the loop's two comparisons as constant. Rather than leaving them in baselines that are meant to be emptied, they are now ignored in `phpstan.neon.dist` with an explanation, and the two baseline files are deleted.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14090.
Follow-up to r58836, r59001, r61699, r63023, r64237.

author: westonruter
message: Emoji: Fix defects in emoji scripts and add type checking. Several defects in `wp-emoji.js` had gone unnoticed because neither emoji script was type checked nor tested: * Since 4.4, the fallback for an emoji image which fails to load has never worked. The `onerror` handler given to Twemoji referred to the library object instead of the image element, leaving a broken image icon in place of the emoji character. * Because that handler never set the `data-error` attribute, the `MutationObserver` guard which recognizes such a replacement was unreachable, hiding the fact that it abandoned all remaining mutation records rather than only the one it recognized. It is corrected along with the handler, since fixing the handler alone would cause an element added in the same batch as a failed image to go unparsed. * An added `` elements inside it. * The `wp-exclude-emoji` class was matched as a substring of the `class` attribute rather than as a class, so classes such as `my-wp-exclude-emoji` also excluded an element. Code which could not run in any browser able to load the script is removed: * The IE 11 workaround. * The `browserSupportsSvgAsImage()` check, whose call to `document.implementation.hasFeature()` always returns `true` per the DOM standard, so the PNG fallback was unreachable. * The vendor-prefixed `MutationObserver` detection. The rest of `wp-emoji.js` is modernized to match the emoji loader, which was already updated in r60899. Both scripts are added to the files checked by `tsc`, with new typings for the settings exported by `_print_emoji_detection_script()`, the vendored Twemoji library, and `WorkerGlobalScope`, which the `dom` lib does not provide. Annotating the loader's support tests precisely made `browserSupportsEmoji()` exhaustively checked, and `allowUnreachableCode` is disabled so that unreachable code is reported on the command line and not just in editors. The first QUnit tests for `wp-emoji.js` are added, covering each defect fixed here. The loader remains untested because it exports nothing and runs on import, leaving no seam to test through. Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/13592. Follow-up to r35637, r36817, r37471, r55186, r60899, r60902. Props westonruter, peterwilsoncc. See #65997, #66033. Fixes #66131.

author: westonruter
message:
Feeds: Fix feed build date for ID-only and partial queries.

When the main query used `fields => 'ids'`, `get_feed_build_date()` passed the integer IDs to `wp_list_pluck()`, which could not read `post_modified_gmt` from them and returned an empty array, so `max()` threw a `ValueError` on PHP 8 and broke the feed. With `fields => 'id=>parent'`, the partial objects lack `post_modified_gmt`, producing a bogus build date. Post IDs and partial objects are now resolved to posts after priming the post cache in a single query, while `WP_Post` objects are read as-is so that virtual posts and in-memory changes are respected. An empty list of modified times now falls back to the last modified time of any post instead of reaching `max()`.

The `have_posts()` check is also removed, since it has side effects: for an empty query it fires the `loop_no_results` action from the feed header before the template's own loop runs, and after a completed loop it fires `loop_end` and rewinds the posts. Comments that a `get_comment` filter returned null for are skipped. These changes also resolve the PHPStan errors that were reported in the function.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/11387.
Follow-up to r44948, r46974.

message:
Posts, Post types: Introduce pre-flight filter to `wp_count_posts()`.

Introduces the pre-flight filter `pre_wp_count_posts` to `wp_count_posts()`.

Returning a non-null value short-circuits `wp_count_posts()`, skipping both the object cache lookup and the database query. This allows the counts to be served from another source, such as a value pre-computed in the background, when an exact real-time count is not required.

Any registered post status missing from the filtered value are added to the result and set to zero.

The returned value is not cached and passed through the `wp_count_posts` filter.

author: afercia
message:
Administration: Improve focus management and screen reader announcements when navigating the media and theme browsers.

In the various media and theme browsers, the announcements for screen readers were sometimes too noisy because focus was set too often and unnecessarily on some elements. To improve the announcements and move focus only when really necessary, all the media and theme browsers are now standardized to the following pattern:

- Makes sure all the media and theme browsers have a dialog role.
- Keeps the navigation buttons focusable by using `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`.
- Ensures that screen reader announcements are cleaner by keeping focus on the activated control rather than moving it to another element.
- Makes sure initial focus is set to the dialog element when it is opened.
- Makes sure to return focus to the opener control when the dialog is closed.
- Makes sure the opener control is a focusable element.
- Adjusts styles accordingly to take the `aria-disabled` attribute into account.
- Simplifies the buttons accessible name to: Previous / Next / Close.
- Makes sure the ARIA live regions are not hidden when they inherit `visibility: hidden`.

Fixes #65746.

author: tyxla
message:
Database: Add `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` to `wpdb::$incompatible_modes`.

When `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` is on, MySQL treats the backslash as a normal character instead of an escape character. WordPress relies on backslash escaping, so queries with escaped values can fail.

`wpdb::set_sql_mode()` now removes this mode from the session, as it already does for the other incompatible modes. Sites that need the mode can still allow it with the `incompatible_sql_modes` filter.

Includes an update to `test_set_incompatible_sql_mode()` to cover the new mode.

author: westonruter
message:
Build/Test Tools: Update PHPStan to 2.3.0.

This also updates `phpstan/phpstan-phpunit` to 2.1.1, which requires PHPStan 2.3. The release analyzes code more precisely, so 12 `variable.undefined` baseline entries no longer match. It also reports two comparisons in `WP_HTML_Processor::run_adoption_agency_algorithm()` as constant: every path through the outer loop body returns or calls `bail()`, so the loop never runs a second time. That loop is scaffolding for parts of the algorithm that are not yet supported, so the comparisons are baselined as work still to do.

PHPStan 2.3 deprecates `ResultCacheMetaExtension`, which `HookDocsResultCacheMetaExtension` implemented to discard the whole result cache whenever a hook docblock inherited through a "This filter is documented in" reference changed. Resolving such a reference now declares each candidate file as a dependency of the file being analyzed, so editing a canonical docblock re-analyzes only the files that inherit it, and the scan of the whole tree that ran on every analysis is gone. The extension also hashed the tooling's own sources, which PHPStan 2.3 already does for every registered extension, so it is removed.

Developed in https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/pull/14089.
Follow-up to r62939, r64012.

Props westonruter, swissspidy.
See #65817.

author: SergeyBiryukov
message:
Code Quality: Remove a no-op assignment of `$addl_path` in `redirect_canonical()`.

`$addl_path` is initialized to an empty string, and the feed branch then sets it to itself with a trailing slash if it is not empty. Since it is always empty at that point, the assignment always results in an empty string and is removed. There is no change in behavior.

This resolves one error in the `empty.variable` PHPStan baseline.
